anomalies.observed: Both ground-domain pins (GND1 and GND2) of each CAN isolation transceiver are connected to the same global GND net.
anomalies.expected: The CAN interfaces are specified as isolated; the transceivers' GND1 and GND2 domains should remain separate, with the bus-side domain powered and grounded independently.

evidence.quote: U37: GND1, GND2; both pins show GND connections. U57: GND1, GND2; both pins show GND connections. (cm4-robot.kicad_sch, page 1, CAN BUS block)
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: Tying the two ground domains together defeats galvanic isolation on both CAN interfaces, allowing ground-potential differences and transients on the bus side to reach the controller-side ground.

parsed.summary: The CAN transceivers' two ground domains are visibly tied to the same GND net, contradicting the specified isolation. This removes galvanic isolation from both CAN interfaces.
